title: Power Pages: performance and usage metrics in the Power Platform admin center monitor hub
summary: The roadmap details and both existing admin paths are supported. However, the briefing treats Monitor access roles, retention limits and enabling controls as unpublished even though the cited Monitor documentation gives platform-wide requirements and limits; those general rules must be distinguished from details still unpublished for Power Pages.

claims.quote:
Session count: Tracks the number of sessions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The identifiers included in the integration's downloadable reports are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "monitor" "reports" identifiers retention; "Power Pages" "monitor hub". Read roadmap and Monitor overview; neither specifies identifiers in the planned Power Pages detailed reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Access presumably follows admin center roles, but the exact role requirements are not published.
claims.quote: Admin experiences are available to Power Platform service and Dynamics 365 admins, who can view Monitor data across the tenant. Makers can view data only for resources that they have edit privileges for in the runtime environment.
claims.fix: Replace the Security & identity bullet with: 'Monitor documentation gives tenant-wide admin access to Power Platform service and Dynamics 365 admins. Viewing resource names requires the environment system administrator role. Any additional Power Pages-specific role requirements are not yet published.' Narrow the corresponding open question to additional Power Pages-specific requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes metrics, trends and report downloads, not autonomous site actions.
claims.quote: Additional capabilities include trend visualization and the ability to download detailed reports for further analysis

claims.where: Cost and licensing: retention limits; Open questions
claims.claim: Retention limits are not yet published.
claims.quote:
Event logs in the monitoring experiences are available for only up to seven days.
- Metrics are available for only up to 28 days.
claims.fix: Replace the retention part of the sentence with: 'Monitor documentation states that event logs are available for up to seven days and metrics for up to 28 days; any Power Pages-specific differences are not yet published.' Narrow the retention open question to Power Pages-specific differences and the contents of downloadable reports.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: Site traffic analytics
claims.claim: Site traffic analytics is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Products > Power Pages > Analytics (preview).
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select **Manage**.
3. Under **Products**, select **Power Pages** and then select **Analytics (preview)**.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for site traffic analytics is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages traffic analytics API Power Platform API pac pages PowerShell analytics; "Power Pages" "analytics" "PowerShell". Read traffic analytics, pac pages, pac power-pages command headings and Power Platform API Websites operations; no equivalent found.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 administrators can access the site traffic analytics dashboard.
claims.quote:
To access the analytics dashboard, you should have one of the following roles:

- Dynamics 365 administrator

claims.claim: Power Platform administrators can access the site traffic analytics dashboard.
claims.quote:
To access the analytics dashboard, you should have one of the following roles:

claims.claim: System administrators can see analytics for the environments where they are system administrators.
claims.quote: System administrator (You can only see environments for which you're a system administrator.)

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: traffic analytics exclude private sites
claims.claim: Existing site traffic reports cover public sites only and exclude private sites.
claims.quote: Traffic reports are available only for public sites. Private sites aren't included in these reports.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: Diagnostic logs for a site
claims.claim: Diagnostic logging is at Power Platform admin center > Resources > Power Pages sites > site > Site Actions > Enable diagnostics logs.
claims.quote:
Under the Resources section, select **Power Pages sites**.
3. Select your website.
4. From the **Site Actions** menu, select **Enable diagnostics logs**.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for enabling site diagnostic logs is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages enable diagnostic logging API PowerShell pac pages diagnostic logs; "Power Pages" "diagnostic" "PowerShell" Enable. Read website error logs, pac pages, pac power-pages command headings and Power Platform API Websites operations; no equivalent found.

claims.claim: Enabling or scoping Power Pages metrics in Monitor has no documented admin UI or automation control.
claims.quote: Tenant-level analytics must be turned on to make data available for Monitor experiences.
claims.fix: Narrow controls[2].governs to 'Power Pages-specific enablement or scoping switch in Monitor' and retain both null sides. Replace its note with: 'No Power Pages-specific switch is documented. Monitor generally requires tenant-level analytics to be enabled.' Add the same qualification to the governance prose, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/monitoring/monitoring-overview. The documented general enablement path is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Tenant settings > Analytics > Tenant-level analytics > Enable > Save at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/tenant-level-analytics; do not describe the general prerequisite as undocumented.

claims.claim: The monitor hub is in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: directly within the monitor hub of the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: The Monitor area calculates health metrics by aggregating runtime logs.
claims.quote: Metrics are calculated by aggregating daily event logs from runtime activity; they're not real-time.

claims.quote: The **Monitor** experience is available to both makers (in experiences such as Power Apps) and admins (in experiences such as the Power Platform admin center).

claims.claim: Monitor provides a reporting surface for operational health.
claims.quote: Your organization can use the **Monitor** area of the Power Platform admin center to measure and improve operational health metrics of resources that are built or deployed.
